title: fix(scripts): check:spec-symbols reads EVERY occurrence of a claim phrase, not the first
body:
Fixes #8819

## What was wrong

`scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs`, `findClaim`: every entry in `CLAIM_PATTERNS` carries `/i` and none carries `/g`, and `exec` was called **once** per pattern. Exactly one occurrence of each phrase per docblock — the first — was ever tested for proximity to an `@objectstack/spec` mention. When that first occurrence failed `CLAIM_WINDOW` or the same-sentence test, the loop moved to the next pattern and every later occurrence of the same phrase went unexamined, including one sitting directly beside a mention.

It fails **permissive**. Two of the twelve patterns are ordinary English in technical prose (`mirror`, `match`), so a declaration that hand-copies a spec symbol and says so passed whenever an innocent earlier occurrence consumed the single `exec` — a silent green on exactly what the rule's own failure text is written against: *"a canonical-sounding comment with nothing behind it is a planted premise for the next session, not stale documentation"*.

## What changed

`findClaim` now walks **every** occurrence of each phrase, via `matchAll`.

⛔ The `/g` deliberately does **not** go on the exported `CLAIM_PATTERNS` literals. `/g` makes `exec` and `test` stateful through `lastIndex`, and `CLAIM_PATTERNS` is a shared module-level array an importer may call either on; the second call would resume mid-string and the gate's verdict would then depend on how many docblocks preceded it. A non-deterministic gate is worse than the first-occurrence bug it would be fixing. Instead a module-private `/g` copy of each pattern is used with `matchAll`, which clones the pattern through the species constructor and never mutates the source — the idiom `MEMBER_CITATION` already uses in this same file — and the copies are private precisely so nothing can `exec` them.

⛔ Tightening toward the already-declared subject, not widening: `CLAIM_PATTERNS` is untouched, `CLAIM_WINDOW` is untouched, no new claim vocabulary. The card is about occurrences, not vocabulary.

## Blast radius — measured, and it is zero

The question the triage seat made item 1: does making every occurrence eligible surface hits the old behaviour was suppressing?

Both scanners were run over the **same** file list with the **same** spec export map (`specExportNames()`, 5085 names), and the `file:line symbol (claim phrase)` verdict sets diffed:

```
files=2322 specNames=5085 before=20 after=20
ADDED (0):
REMOVED (0):
```

The file list is a deliberate **superset** of the gate's own — 2322 files against the gate's 1384, because the probe omitted the gate's `.test.` / `.stories.` exclusion. Zero added on the wider population.

The gate's verdict line is byte-identical before and after:

```
spec symbol derivation: 1384 files scanned against 5085 spec export names; 18 declared dialects, 0 untriaged collisions in 0 packages.
spec alignment claims: 2 declared deliberate copies, 18 unbacked claims in 5 packages.
spec member citations: 1384 sources + 184 documentation pages; nothing cites a key its spec symbol does not declare.
```

⇒ **0 docblocks newly fail.** No existing docblock needs repairing, so the mass-edit branch the dispatch guarded against does not open. ⭐ The masking **condition** is demonstrated; an actually **escaped** claim on this tree is measured at zero — which the card itself said had not been measured, and is the reading that would justify resizing this to p3.

## The instrument discriminates — this is a reading, not a dead probe

A zero delta is only worth anything if the probe could have moved. The new fixture is the acceptance the dispatch asked for: an innocent early "mirror images" far from any mention, and a real claim (`mirrors @objectstack/spec ListView roots exactly`) beside a mention later in the same block.

One-shot ablation, on the committed fix, restoring `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` from the branch point and running the same command:

```
MUTATION ON DISK: head=88006305fd8dd62ecd4828ed0e4352b9104209a0 mutated=eb03a2f45bcab189f8aa3502d495c2a256b7f62e
occurrence-loop present in mutated file: 0  (expect 0)
Tests  3 failed | 2 passed | 69 skipped (74)
```

and on the fix: `Tests  74 passed (74)`. Restore verified by `git diff HEAD` empty and by blob hash, not by an exit code.

The 2 that pass under **both** scanners are the controls, and they are the point:

- the same block with the innocent early occurrence deleted is flagged by both ⇒ the claim half is real and the masking is the only difference;
- the `/g`-free pin on `CLAIM_PATTERNS` holds under both ⇒ it pins the design, not the change.

## The card's own worked example, re-verified on this tree

`ROW_PREDICATE_ROOTS` in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ConditionalFormattingEditor.tsx` still reads "They were mirror images" and "a condition that silently never matches", and still carries a single `@objectstack/spec` mention far from both. It is a live instance of the masking condition. It is **not** a live escape: nothing later in that block places a claim phrase beside the mention, which is why it is unchanged here and why the verdict set did not move.

## Gates

| command | exit |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm check:spec-symbols` | 0 |
| `npx vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-spec-symbol-derivation.test.ts` + the 6 `spec-symbol-ledger-*-7265` suites (every importer of the module) | 0 — 160 passed |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 |
| `pnpm lint:root` | 0 — full scope, not narrowed; 0 errors, 32 pre-existing warnings |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:shell-escape-residue` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | 0 |
| `pnpm check:changeset-claims` | 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 — its own verdict: *"No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed."* |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` (both paths) | 0 — NOT GOVERNED, ordinary review route |

`pnpm lint` (turbo, per package) is not owed: the diff touches only `scripts/`, which the per-package lint tasks do not walk, and type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.js` (no `project` / `projectService`), so nothing in this diff can move the verdict on a file it does not touch.

⛔ `skip-changeset` is a phantom label in this repo and was not applied. No labels were written at all.

## Acceptance notes

- Out-of-scope observation, **noted, not filed**: `memberCitationsIn` in the same file already walks every occurrence (`matchAll` over a shared `/g` `MEMBER_CITATION`), so rule 4 never had this defect — the two halves of the file now agree, and there is nothing to file. Successor: this PR.
